title: NCCDFI 2026 – Day 1 concludes in New Delhi, Strengthening India's Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics Ecosystem
subtitle:
NIELIT Launches Digital Applications viz. CyberVitals  and Netअन्वेषक at NCCDFI 2026
Kick-off of Cyber Kushti 2026 – Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon
body_text: The National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, successfully concluded the Day 1 of the 3 rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) on 16 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. Day 1 of the NCCDFI 2026 under the theme “Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India's Digital Future,” brought together policymakers, senior government officials, law enforcement agencies, defence personnel, judicial representatives, cybersecurity professionals, industry leaders, researchers and academicians to deliberate on the evolving cybersecurity landscape and the growing challenges of digital crime and investigations. The conference was inaugurated by Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT) & Honourable Vice-Chancellor, NIELIT Deemed to be University , as the Chief Guest, in the august presence of distinguished dignitaries; Shri Rupin Sharma, IPS, DGP Nagaland; Dr. Sandeep Mittal, IPS, DGP & Chairman, TNUSRB, Government of Tamil Nadu; Ms. A. Pratibha, Economic Advisor, MeitY; Shri Sridhar CV, Mission Director, Andhra Pradesh State Quantum Mission (APSQM), GoAP;  Shri Atul Tripathi, Honorary Adjunct Fellow at National Maritime Foundation and Shri L Lanuwabang, Director, NIELIT Kohima. The inaugural session of the 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) commenced with a welcome address by Shri L Lanuwabang, that had set the tone for the two-day national conference. The welcome note highlighted NCCDFI's journey from Kohima (2024) to Guwahati (2025) and New Delhi (2026), acknowledging the leadership of Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, NIELIT. He emphasised on the need for collective action, institutional collaboration and innovation to address emerging cyber threats. The conference spreads over seven technical sessions, over 30 speakers and 12 industry partners, aiming to strengthen India's cybersecurity and digital forensics capabilities towards building a Cyber Secure Bharat . In the inaugural address by Chief Guest, Prof. (Dr.) M. M. Tripathi, Director General, National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT) & Honourable Vice-Chancellor, NIELIT Deemed to be University , he emphasised that cybersecurity has evolved beyond IT into a critical national priority, encompassing law enforcement, banking stability, critical infrastructure, public trust and national security. He highlighted NIELIT's key initiatives, including ICSAS, Live Website Acquisition Tool, Cyber Crime Management System and CyberDaksh , an AI-powered assistant being developed to support cybercrime investigators. He also announced NIELIT Deemed-to-be University's initiative to establish a dedicated Quantum and Artificial Intelligence University campus at Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh , envisioned as a centre for advanced education, research and innovation in these emerging technologies. He emphasized upon three priorities: PRIORITY 1 - BUILD OUR OWN TECHNOLOGY - NIELIT's efforts to develop indigenous cybersecurity solutions, including ICSAS, Live Website Acquisition Tool, Cyber Crime Management System and CyberDaksh. He emphasised India's need to become a technology creator rather than merely a consumer, while strengthening capabilities in AI, semiconductors, electronics, digital forensics and other emerging technologies. PRIORITY 2 - BUILD PEOPLE AND NATIONAL SKILLS - NIELIT's role in addressing the national skill gap through industry-aligned education, specialised training and digital learning. Key initiatives include B.Tech, M.Tech and Ph.D. programmes, the proposed Quantum and AI University campus at Amaravati, NIELIT Digital University with over 3.70 lakh enrolments, and semiconductor ATMP training facilities in Ahmedabad and Guwahati. He also emphasised strengthening cybersecurity and digital forensics skills among police, judiciary, armed forces and government officials to build a future-ready workforce. PRIORITY 3 - BUILD A STRONG NATIONAL ECOSYSTEM - the importance of building a strong national cybersecurity ecosystem through collaboration among government agencies, law enforcement, academia and industry. He highlighted the signing of MoUs at NCCDFI 2026 to promote institutional partnerships and practical outcomes. Shri Rupin Sharma, highlighted NCCDFI's journey from Kohima to Guwahati and New Delhi, appreciating NIELIT Kohima's support in strengthening Nagaland Police's cyber-forensic capabilities, specialised training and digital recruitment systems. Dr. Sandeep Mittal, highlighted that human beings remain the weakest link in the cybersecurity ecosystem, whether they are end users, software developers or system administrators. He also congratulated NIELIT on organising a successful and insightful conference, and appreciated NIELIT's efforts in undertaking a large-scale Faculty Development Programme (FDP) across the country. Ms. A. Pratibha, highlighted India's efforts to strengthen its cybersecurity ecosystem through large-scale skill development, institutional capacity building, and coordinated cyber threat response. She also stressed that technical expertise must be supported by ethics, privacy, and responsible technology practices to achieve Cyber Secure Bharat, Viksit Bharat 2047, and Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Shri Sridhar CV, highlighted the critical role of NIELIT in promoting cybersecurity awareness and capacity building across the country. He noted that NIELIT has trained more than 1.6 crore individuals, including a significant number in the domain of cybersecurity. He emphasised that while substantial investments are being made in developing digital infrastructure and advanced technologies, equal attention must be given to securing these assets by fostering a strong cybersecurity mindset. Shri Atul Tripathi, in his address emphasized that cybersecurity begins with individual awareness and responsibility. In an increasingly interconnected world, our personal data, digital footprints, and online behaviour can become vulnerabilities exploited by cybercriminals and adversaries. Practising good cyber hygiene, protecting sensitive information, avoiding oversharing on social media, and creating awareness among vulnerable communities are essential to strengthening our collective security. Dr. Alok Tripathi, Director (Scheme/Skilling), NIELIT, delivered the Vote of Thanks, expressing his gratitude to the distinguished dignitaries, eminent cybersecurity professionals, representatives from law enforcement agencies, academia and industry, speakers, researchers, delegates, members of the media and NIELIT colleagues for their valuable participation and contributions to the conference. The conference witnessed the signing of MoUs between NIELIT and various partner organisations, marking a significant step towards fostering institutional and industry collaboration. The agreements seek to promote joint research, technology development, specialised training and knowledge sharing in cybersecurity and related emerging technology domains. The organisations with which MoUs were exchanged are Bhasha Interface for India (BHASHINI); Anuvadini – AI-Based Translation Platform, InGage Technologies, QuNu Labs Private Limited, IBM India, Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH), and Pan IIT Alumni Foundation. The conference also witnessed the launch of new digital applications by NIELIT viz. CyberVitals and Net अन्वेषक ; and kick-off of Cyber Kushti 2026 – Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon , aimed at fostering innovation, practical problem-solving and technical excellence among aspiring cybersecurity professionals through challenges centred on Review, Attack and Defend . CyberVitals mobile app is a cybersecurity and privacy suite that detects risky permissions, malware, unsafe app sources, outdated apps, and potential security threats. It also analyzes images for AI-generated content and provides trust scores for better verification. Real-time network, app activity, and notification monitoring helps identify suspicious behaviour while keeping user data private. Net अन्वेषक , the Network Explorer developed by NIELIT Gorakhpur is an in-house Network Administration Suite for device discovery, network monitoring, security assessment and diagnostics through a single application. It also offers tools for port scanning, PC security analysis, uptime monitoring and network troubleshooting. An industry exhibition was also organised as part of the conference, showcasing advanced technologies, products and solutions in cybersecurity, digital forensics, drone technology, surveillance systems and AI-driven security. 12 industry partners along with knowledge partners, showcased innovative technologies, products and solutions in cybersecurity and digital forensics. The exhibition facilitated technology demonstrations, networking and collaboration among industry stakeholders, experts and delegates.  The exhibitors include, Telangana Cyber Security Bureau, ADF Solutions, Vertexon Labs, Stellar, 4n6care Technologies Pvt. Ltd., 3rd Eye Techno Solutions, MSAB, Magnet Forensics, CyberPeace, Cellebrite, ISAC, and Forensicsguru, besides NIELIT Ropar (NDU) & NIELIT Deemed to be University, NIELIT Kohima and NIELIT Gorakhpur.  The exhibition provided an interactive platform for technology demonstrations, knowledge exchange and networking among industry partners, government agencies, students and other stakeholders. The conference featured a series of technical sessions, expert talks and panel discussions covering critical areas such as Artificial Intelligence-driven cyber threats, digital forensics, critical infrastructure protection, cyber intelligence, incident response, blockchain security, cloud security, digital evidence, cyber law and emerging technologies. Experts from government agencies, law enforcement, defence establishments, academia and the technology industry shared their insights, experiences and perspectives on addressing contemporary cybersecurity challenges. Through this platform, NIELIT reaffirms its commitment to support the Government of India's vision of a secure, resilient and digitally empowered nation. **** Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma
